clue.text: Cold girl's place in the sun?

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Anne is a girl's name, and the possessive gives ANNE'S

explanation.surface: A chilly young woman wonders where she might find a sunny spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: this resort on the French Riviera is literally a place in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera resort is famed for sunshine and beaches, a sunny holiday destination.

clue.text: Regularly sees church supporting solid fuel blend

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so church comes below

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word sees

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church sees a mix of solid fuels burnt on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'sees', giving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge or come together into one mass is to fuse.

clue.text: Black mark for venue providing entertainment

parts.note: night is black, the dark hours
a spot is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: A dark stain on the reputation of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub or evening venue offering music and shows.

clue.text: Bird described in modern English

indicators.note: described in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird written about in contemporary English prose.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: A lover's head drops on west of Marshall islands

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the run A, L, DIVES follows the Marshall letter
in an across clue the west of a word is its leftmost, opening letter
the head of the word lover's is its opening letter

parts.note: drops in the sense of plunges, falls headlong

explanation.surface: A romantic swoons somewhere near the Marshall Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts A + L + DIVES after the M from 'west of Marshall'. 'Marshall islands' looks like one name, but 'islands' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian Ocean nation is an archipelago of coral atolls, a chain of islands.

clue.text: Changed for a private date, after a day

indicators.note: after means the run from a private date follows the run from a day

parts.note: Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private

explanation.surface: A soldier rearranges his plans for a date, a day later.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a private date' pieces give APTED; 'after a day' puts them behind A + D.
explanation.definitionFit: Altered to suit new conditions, modified.

clue.text: Would it keep a wet Ascot dry?

definitions.text: Would it keep a wet Ascot dry?

parts.words: Would it keep a wet Ascot dry?
parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, so a soggy Ascot would be a soaked racetrack; the real thing is the waterproof layer in a wall that keeps rising moisture out

explanation.surface: Wondering what could protect the Royal Ascot races from rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire; read the answer as 'a wet course' and it describes a rained-on Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof barrier built into a wall to stop moisture rising from the ground.

clue.text: Sort of consonant put in novel arrangement

indicators.note: put in says the answer is placed within the words novel arrangement

explanation.surface: A kind of consonant introduced in a new layout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound made with the back of the tongue against the soft palate, as in k or g.

clue.text: Elder Spanish gentleman has to eat one

indicators.note: has to eat means takes a piece inside, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: señor is the Spanish for a gentleman, Mr
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An older Spaniard is obliged to eat something.
explanation.definitionFit: Older in years or higher in rank.

clue.text: Poor old-timers losing set address

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of old-timers are in a bad state and must be reworked

explanation.surface: Impoverished veterans lose their fixed home address.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of 'set' ('losing') from 'old-timers' and rearrange the remainder. 'Address' is a form of address, not a street location.
explanation.definitionFit: An old courtly way of speaking to a nobleman, a form of salutation.

clue.text: Country cooking range — metal one

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of range are being worked over and mixed into a new order

parts.note: tin is a metal
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A kitchen inventory: a stove and something made of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges RANGE to ARGEN; the cooker 'range' in the surface is really just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American republic is a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Theologian dismissed from Midland city

indicators.note: dismissed from says these letters are sent away out of the word Midland

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the degree of a theologian

explanation.surface: A scholar of religion is sacked by a firm in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ds removed are scattered: one from the start of 'Midland' and one from its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern Italian fashion capital is a major urban centre.

clue.text: Food available in The Wheatsheaf?

indicators.note: available in says the answer can be found sitting inside the words The Wheatsheaf

explanation.surface: A pub called The Wheatsheaf advertises that it serves meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wheatsheaf is a common British pub name, so the surface asks whether this pub does food.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for things to eat, snacks and meals.

clue.text: Place where Cameron lot get excited?

indicators.note: get excited suggests the letters of Cameron lot are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Where would a British prime minister's set become thrilled?
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron is David Cameron, former UK prime minister; the casino town is a fitting place for such a crowd to get excited.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monaco resort is a district famous for its casino, a location.

clue.text: Sort of travel firm our times perhaps welcomes

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the firm goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests the letters of our times might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company perhaps embraces a type of travel for the modern age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OUR TIMES to ETOURISM, and CO goes in after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourism aimed at protecting the natural environment is a kind of holidaying.

clue.text: East coast resort to limit European fish

parts.note: to cap is to limit or put a ceiling on
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A seaside town considers restricting European fishing catches.
explanation.walkthrough: East coast here means the Atlantic coast of the United States: the Massachusetts peninsula is a holiday area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts peninsula is a summer holiday destination on America's Atlantic shore.

clue.text: Manages, welcoming American wets

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: does in the sense of gets by, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A boss copes well with visiting Americans who are drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak or drench something with water is to make it wet.

clue.text: Cathedral city welcoming reason, with feeling

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: A cathedral city welcomes logic with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in eastern England, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a way that stirs emotion, passionately.

clue.text: One who evaluates sulphur in fools' gold!

indicators.note: in places the sulphur letter within the fools and gold run

parts.note: asses are fools
or is gold in heraldry
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Fool's gold is iron pyrites, which contains sulphur.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to fool's gold (iron pyrites, an iron sulphide). OR is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraiser who values property or judges performance.

clue.text: Standing of university in branch of maths

indicators.note: in places the university letter within the name of the branch of maths

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, is a branch of mathematics

explanation.surface: A university's reputation for its statistics department.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's standing is their rank or position in society.

clue.text: Gazed across river and took the lead part

indicators.note: across means one piece spans the other, which therefore goes inside

parts.note: stared means gazed

explanation.surface: Someone stared over a river and then played the main role.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been the principal performer in a film or play.

clue.text: Copper finally understands cats' habits

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word understands

parts.note: toms are male cats

explanation.surface: A police officer eventually grasps what cats habitually do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are established practices or traditions, ways of doing things.

clue.text: Sinister member of the Lords put up in empty cemetery

indicators.note: in places the reversed peer within the emptied cemetery
empty means remove the inside, leaving only the first and last letters of cemetery
put up in a down clue means written upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: A ghostly scene of a lord's body laid out in a deserted graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' means written upwards in this down clue; 'empty' strips the cemetery to its outer letters, and the lord sits inside that shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie and unsettling, causing a shiver of fear.

clue.text: Angel's turn of phrase

indicators.note: turn of suggests the letters of phrase are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A heavenly being has a gift for an elegant expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn of phrase' looks like a set idiom, but 'turn of' is the anagram signal on PHRASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A celestial being of the highest order in the heavenly hierarchy.

clue.text: Groups accompanying surgeon eat with abandon

indicators.note: with abandon suggests the letters of surgeon eat are flung about without restraint

explanation.surface: A doctor tucks into a meal wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinues are bands of attendants or followers travelling with an important person.

clue.text: North played badly — a problem in one's side

indicators.note: played badly suggests the letters of North are mishandled into a new order

explanation.surface: North, a bridge player, had a poor game, causing trouble for the partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North is a player position; the definition draws on the idiom 'a thorn in one's side'.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom of a persistent irritant, a prickle lodged in the flesh.

clue.text: Expense initially allocated to victory tipple

indicators.note: allocated to means the expense letter is assigned and attached to the end of victory

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word Expense

explanation.surface: The cost of a celebratory drink after a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, such as a glass of something from grapes.

clue.text: Discreet attention seeker?

parts.note: an attention seeker is usually loud, but this one is a quiet hissing sound made to catch someone's notice

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to be noticed but quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered sibilant sound people make to get someone's attention without raising their voice.

clue.text: Oil blended in first-class garlic dip

indicators.note: in places the blended letters within the first-class symbol

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as the letters AI

indicators.note: blended suggests the letters of Oil are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A top-quality garlic dip made with mixed-in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common way of saying first-class, written in crosswords with the letter I standing in for the digit 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The Provençal mayonnaise flavoured with garlic is served as a sauce for dipping.

clue.text: Seize assets of English hunting parties in case of redress

indicators.note: in places English and hunting parties within the case of redress
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: posses are groups gathered to hunt down a fugitive

explanation.surface: Bailiffs confiscate the property of English hunts in order to obtain compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of redress' gives R and S, the first and last letters of 'redress', which go round E + POSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back goods or property when payments have lapsed is to reclaim them.

clue.text: Personally developed cheese sent back by worker

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in a farmhand

indicators.note: sent back means the cheese is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A labourer returns some cheese that was made by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns EDAM into MADE; 'by' just places it beside HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crafted by an individual rather than a machine is personally produced.

clue.text: Tabloid accepts the old horse with stamina

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Star is a British tabloid newspaper
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A tabloid paper takes on a veteran racehorse that never tires.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Star is a British tabloid. YE is an old way of writing 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing a stayer is a horse that runs best over long distances, needing endurance.
